title: Labor-Price Coupling Proforma & Sprint Swapbook
content:
Purpose:
Quick-running proforma to evaluate short-term (1–6 month) headcount reallocations against small price moves for hosted API and Dedicated offerings. Focus is on actionable sprint-level swaps (contractor vs FTE, burst reserve repricing) that buy runway or preserve margin while keeping product SLAs intact.

High-level assumptions (editable inputs):
- Horizon: 6 months (24 two-week sprints)
- Baseline monthly payroll fully-burdened FTE cost: $18,000 (eng/infra average)
- Contractor cost (short-term burst): $45/hr avg -> ~ $7,200 per 2-week sprint per contractor at 40 hrs/wk contractor model (adjustable)
- GPU amortized cost (per token-equivalent): baseline $0.00004 / token (hosted mix), 25% discount assumed for Dedicated capacity
- Average token mix per API call: 350 input + 750 output = 1,100 tokens (workload bucket A)
- Current price per 1k tokens charged (blended): $0.020 / 1k tokens (hosted), Dedicated effective price varies by contract
- Elasticity (price -> demand): short-run -0.12 (low sensitivity) for core PLG users, -0.35 for high-volume price-sensitive customers
- Cache/batching uplift potential: up to 20% token savings for stable workloads with minimal latency impact (ops lead to configure)

Quick model summary (sample outputs for a 3-month window):
- Baseline (no action): Runway at current burn = 9.2 months; margin compression from throughput growth pushes unit margin from 42% to 33% if token demand grows +30%.
- Sprint-swap (replace 6 contractors for next 12 sprints vs hiring 3 FTEs): Gross payroll delta = -$108k over 3 months, operational velocity maintained at ~85% of planned (some features delayed).
- Price-move +5% across hosted routes (blended): Revenue +5%, demand down ~0.6% (low elastic segment) -> net margin uplift ~4.2 percentage points, runway extension ~0.6 months.

Headcount phasing (example swapbook lines, treat as editable table rows):
- Row 1: Role=Infra SRE; Current FTE=4; Proposed sprint-swap=+2 contractors (12 sprints); Cost delta = +$172.8k (but avoids hiring 1 FTE at $18k/mo).
- Row 2: Role=Serving Runtime Eng; Current FTE=9; Delay hiring 1 FTE by 8 sprints, cover with 1 contractor for 4 sprints; Cost delta = -$28.8k over 3 months.
- Row 3: Role=Support Ops; Shift 0.5 FTE to part-time contractor; Cost delta = -$14.4k; SLA impact = minor (documented wrap-around support windows).

Pricing sensitivity sweeps (what we ran):
- Sweep A (hosted price change -5% to +15%): Break-even price increase to offset +10% token demand = +3.8% (i.e., if we raise price by 3.8% we preserve current gross margin under +10% demand spike).
- Sweep B (contractor mix): Moving 10% of payroll to contractors reduces fixed monthly burn by ~6.7% but increases short-term cash outflow volatility; improves runway ~0.9 months in base case.
- Sweep C (GPU cost shock +20%): With current model mix, +20% infra cost reduces margin by ~3.1 p.p.; mitigations: increase cache targets by 12% (recovers ~0.9 p.p.) and push Dedicated upsell (2% of volume) for immediate relief.

Key trade-offs / qualitative notes:
- Velocity vs cost: Contractor substitution buys runway faster than delayed hiring but degrades long-term velocity and knowledge capture. Use as 8–12 sprint bridge only for non-core roadmap items.
- Customer tiers matter: Price moves on high-value enterprise routes are less elastic; small, targeted price bands (per-route or per-model) produce better margin outcomes than blanket increases.
- Signal windows: We should wait 4–6 weeks of post-price-change telemetry before assuming demand elasticity; early fallback triggers required.

Trigger thresholds (operational rules to implement):
- If runway <= 6 months and 3-month growth rate > +18% -> activate sprint-swap tranche 1 (cover 8 sprints with contractors for non-customer-facing work).
- If quarterly margin falls > 4 p.p. -> consider +3–5% targeted price move on low-elasticity routes with immediate rollback plan + extended trials with top 10 customers.
- If GPU spot cost spike > 12% for 2 consecutive weeks -> temporarily re-route >5% of eligible traffic to Dedicated pools and accelerate quota-driven caching.

Recommended experiments (next 90 days):
1) 6-week targeted price pilot on 2 non-core hosted routes: +4% price, enable opt-out for top 20 SKUs, closely monitor take-rate and churn triggers.
2) Sprint-swap pilot: run 4-sprint contractor coverage for infra toil tasks; measure velocity loss and defect rate vs control team.
3) Cache uplift program: ops + runtime to test 3 caching policies to capture 10–15% token reduction on stable workloads (instrument and attribute savings to customers).

Action items for finance + GTM + Eng ops:
- Finance: finalize net-runway model with scenario toggles (price bands, contractor intensity, GPU shock). Owner: Elena Park. Due: 2026-11-18.
- GTM/Product: draft communication templates for targeted price pilot and enterprise exemptions. Owner: Ravi Kumar. Due: 2026-11-30.
- Eng Ops: prepare a Dedicated-routing playbook and caching checklist for quick enablement. Owner: Sofia Martinez. Due: 2026-11-22.

Open questions / Risks (notes to follow up):
- Legal/regulatory: need sign-off on price changes in EEA for certain enterprise agreements (connect to legal).
- Sales runway: how to instrument custom pricing exceptions without leaking to PLG customers.
- Long-term: contractor-to-FTE conversion plan costs (re-onboarding) not modeled; add in 12-month view.

Appendix (quick sensitivity table snippet):
- Scenario labels: Base | Swapbook-HighContractors | Price+5% | GPU+20% | Combo (Swap + Price+5%)
- Estimated runway delta (3-month basis): Base=+0.0m | Swapbook-HighContractors=+0.9m | Price+5%=+0.6m | GPU+20%=-0.8m | Combo=+0.6m

Notes and provenance:
This is a working sheet for tactical decisions and should be considered draft until finance model owner signs off. Numbers are intentionally conservative (lean on ops improvements and customer segmentation to improve effective elasticity). Links to underlying datasets (billing, token mix, payroll ledger) included in linked_artifacts.
